summary: Team weighs delaying launch vs hitting marketing dates
title: Product launch debate

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: I think we should push the launch to next month so the onboarding flow is solid

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: But marketing already booked the campaign slots, what would we tell them exactly?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: We tell them a rushed launch hurts more than a delayed one, remember last quarter

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Fair point, though what is the minimum we could ship without embarrassing ourselves?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Probably the core dashboard and the export feature, everything else can wait

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Okay so how do we decide what counts as core versus nice to have here?

summary: Doctor sees a patient about three weeks of right knee pain
title: Patient visit - knee pain

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Good morning, what brings you in today?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Morning. It's my right knee, it's been aching for about three weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: How long has it been bothering you like this, and is it getting worse?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: About three weeks, and definitely worse after my shifts, I'm on my feet all day.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Any swelling, or does it ever lock up on you?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: It swelled up pretty badly last Tuesday, that's when I got worried.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Are you taking anything for it right now?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Just ibuprofen, 400 milligrams when it gets bad in the evening.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: On a scale of one to ten, where is the pain by end of day?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Like a six out of ten by evening, sometimes I can't sleep on that side.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: I'm going to order an X-ray and refer you to physiotherapy to start.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Could this be arthritis? My mother had it quite young.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: We'll see what the imaging shows before we talk about that, no need to jump ahead.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Will I need surgery, do you think?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Let's have you back in three weeks and see how it responds to physio first.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Okay, thank you doctor.

summary: Blood pressure follow-up; dizziness since lisinopril dose increase
title: BP med review

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Morning, Mr. Ellis - you're here for the blood pressure follow-up?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: That's right. Though since you raised the lisinopril to 20 mg, I've been getting dizzy most mornings.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Dizzy how - lightheaded when you stand up, or the room spinning?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Lightheaded standing up. It passes after a minute or two, but it worries me.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Are you taking it every morning, same time?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Every morning with breakfast. I did miss last Thursday, if that matters.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Any swelling, cough, or palpitations since the change?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: No, nothing like that. I do take ibuprofen now and then for my back.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Okay. Readings are still a touch high, so here's the plan: we'll drop the lisinopril back to 10 mg daily and add amlodipine 5 mg.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Should I be worried the dizziness means something serious?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: With the timing it lines up with the dose increase, which is reassuring - but let's get a basic metabolic panel to be thorough.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: And the ibuprofen - keep taking it?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Sparingly, and not on an empty stomach. I'd like to see you back in four weeks to check the new regimen.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Got it. See you then.
